content:
Installed capacity alone is not enough to assess insurance for a small hydropower plant. The owner needs to describe the buildings, equipment, location, connection to the electricity network and consequences of a production shutdown separately. Low water flow, a damaged turbine and damage to a building are different situations. A policy's general name does not establish that they have the same solution or that an insurer will accept each risk.

This article helps project managers in the Republic of Moldova organise information for a risk review. It does not confirm that an offer is available for every site or establish technical or licensing requirements. Qualified specialists must assess the installation's operation and safety. Insurance ING Broker SRL acts as an insurance broker. The insurer decides whether to accept the risk and determines policy terms and the handling of claims.

What inventory should the assessment start with?

Divide the facility into identifiable categories: the process building, turbine, generator, automation equipment, transformer and other components actually present. Add hydraulic structures only where they form part of the ownership or responsibility being assessed. Do not include another operator's assets without explaining the contractual relationship. An inconsistent inventory may conceal both missing components and values counted twice.

For each item, prepare its identification, installation year, supporting valuation document and known condition. Distinguish the equipment price from transport, installation and commissioning costs. Do not assume that a total book value is automatically the appropriate sum for every insurance contract. Ask for an explanation of the valuation basis and update the list when a component is replaced or the plant's configuration changes.

A location is more than an address

Use the project documents to describe the relationship between buildings, water and access for intervention teams. Relevant general information is enough for an initial discussion. Do not publish security plans, vulnerable points or details enabling unauthorised access. If an assessor requests sensitive technical documents, agree on the transmission channel and authorised recipients before providing them.

Identify which information the project documents confirm and which points require a new inspection. A photograph taken in favourable weather does not demonstrate how the site behaves under all conditions. Retain available reports and the incident history. The absence of a known incident is not evidence that the facility has no flood, landslide or other natural hazard exposure.

Construction project or operating installation?

State the actual stage: construction, installation, testing, acceptance or operation. Where some sections are complete and others remain under construction, describe them separately. Documents for an operating installation should not be presumed suitable for every installation or testing activity. Request a review of the relevant periods and operations instead of inferring protection from the equipment purchase date.

Prepare relevant acceptance records and a list of unfinished work. A partial acceptance or an outstanding technical recommendation must be disclosed accurately. The broker does not certify completion or replace the technical professional responsible. For an insurance assessment, the submitted description needs to match the present situation rather than a planned stage that the project has not yet reached.

Equipment failure and insufficient water flow mean different things

Equipment may be functional while operating conditions affect production. Conversely, operating conditions may be normal but a component damaged. Keep the cause, observed defect and financial consequence distinct. Do not describe every fall in energy output as material damage or assume that every departure from budget can be insured.

When discussing a possible policy with its provider, describe separate scenarios. Ask what event would need to occur before a cost or loss could be considered. Record the answer and the document confirming it. Without confirmation, leave the question open. An optimistic commercial forecast does not change a contract's definitions, exclusions or conditions.

Maintenance, spare parts and reliance on suppliers

Collect service reports and the schedule of planned interventions. Identify spare parts whose procurement may affect shutdown duration. Do not invent delivery times or assume that the manufacturer keeps every component in stock. For internal planning, distinguish confirmed information from the team's estimates and record who can update the information when something changes.

Identify the maintenance provider and the services specified in its contract. Response time to a request is not necessarily the time needed to restore operation. A supplier's warranty, service contract and insurance serve different purposes. Compare them against specific problems without assuming that one replaces the need to review the other two or removes every expense for the owner.

The grid connection and interruptions outside the plant

Describe the operational connection to the network and relevant documents without publishing sensitive diagrams. An external interruption and an internal breakdown should not automatically be treated alike. Moldelectrica publishes information on service quality and continuity indicators. This provides general context, not proof of the cause of an individual interruption or the company's entitlement to compensation under a policy.

For the insurance review, ask explicitly about the plant's own assets and the effects of a problem at another operator. Do not assume that a partner's policy transfers to the plant owner. Retain communications and records concerning the interruption. Contractual responsibility between operators and insurance conditions must be checked separately from measuring energy that could not be delivered.

How should you describe the consequences of a shutdown?

Build a planning scenario showing the stages of recovery: initial assessment, access, diagnosis, procurement and repair, using information from specialists. This article does not provide technical intervention instructions. Its purpose is to identify documents that can support estimates of time and expense. Every assumption needs to be visible to the person using the calculation.

Separate planned revenue, continuing expenses and possible additional costs. Do not simply add them together without checking whether an amount already appears elsewhere. If business interruption insurance is being considered, ask for the triggering event, relevant period and calculation method to be explained. This article does not state that all undelivered energy or every loss of income is included.

Which conditions should you compare before the price?

The premium is the amount paid for insurance. The deductible is the part of a loss borne by the insured under the contract. Also check the assets, defined risks, limits and exclusions, meaning situations for which the contract provides no cover. Ask about provisions that do not match the plant's configuration or the project's actual stage.

Use the same description for all proposals being compared. If one option uses a different inventory or period, flag the difference before comparing amounts. Ask about breakdown assessment, the expert's access and documents needed for notification. A commercial presentation or telephone conversation does not, by itself, amend the policy wording or its annexes.

Illustrative example: a component with a long procurement period

A plant manager identifies only one known supplier for an important module. The manager requests information about diagnosis, an indicative delivery period and documents needed to identify the part. This editorial example does not describe an actual customer. It confirms neither a breakdown nor its technical cause or payment of any cost through insurance. It shows how to describe a dependency before estimating its financial consequences.

The team separates the module's price from other intervention costs and updates the shutdown scenario. The risk review file retains supplier responses and points still unconfirmed. An indicative period is not presented as a firm commitment, and the installation is not altered to simplify documentation. A specialist addresses the technical solution, while policy explanations are requested using the same factual information.

A useful checklist before speaking with the broker

  • The owner, user and actual project stage.
  • The inventory of buildings, structures and equipment being assessed.
  • Documents supporting values, acceptance and important modifications.
  • Incident history and unresolved technical questions.
  • Service contracts and supplier dependencies.
  • Shutdown scenarios, with assumptions and supporting records kept separately.
  • Financier or partner requirements needing clarification.
  • Sensitive information requiring an agreed transmission channel.

Keeping the assessment useful after equipment changes

Replacing the generator, rebuilding automation or changing the maintenance company may mean that the old file no longer describes the plant. Keep a change log identifying the date, affected asset, acceptance document and person updating the inventory. Not all technical documentation needs to circulate outside the operations team. An initial insurance discussion may require only a summary without sensitive details.

At the annual review, also check discontinued spare parts, equipment transferred between sites and work not yet accepted. A recent photograph may show an item's appearance but does not certify its technical condition. A specialist's report and maintenance documents serve a different purpose from a file illustration. Keeping this distinction clear helps the owner avoid presenting an assumption as a finding.

Discuss planned production changes separately from investments actually completed. An extension approved in the budget is not yet an installed asset. For ordered but undelivered equipment, record the project stage and relevant contract. Do not automatically combine it with assets already in operation.

Frequently asked questions about hydropower and insurance

Is there one identical policy for every small hydropower plant?

Do not assume so. Configuration, location, project stage and company documents require individual review. This article does not confirm a solution available for every facility in the Republic of Moldova.

Is low water flow the same as turbine failure?

No. These are different situations requiring separate descriptions and discussion. Their treatment under an insurance contract cannot be inferred from reduced production; the relevant conditions must be checked.

What amount should be entered in an application?

Prepare the inventory and supporting valuation records, then request an explanation of the valuation basis. Do not automatically use book value or the project's historical cost as a universal answer for every asset category.

Can I send plant diagrams and access details through a form?

Do not submit passwords, control access or sensitive plans through a public form. Start with a general description and establish which information is necessary, who needs it and the appropriate transmission channel.
